BLOCKING — F23 (P1, OPEN, NEW, raised by the tenth PR #325 Copilot review of HEAD 914cb214, AFTER the 3-cycle plan-review budget was exhausted). ONE OF THIS TASK'S REQUIRED TESTS IS UNSATISFIABLE AS SPECIFIED.

DEFECT: this task's test list includes `cancel during launch`. Plan §3.2 defines exactly ONE cancellation edge — `RUNNING —(operator cancel)→ CANCELLING` — and Rule 1 states that transitions outside the table are rejected with `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION`. A cancel request arriving while the session is in `LAUNCHING` can therefore only be REFUSED. That directly contradicts the cancellation contract stated in this very task ("operator cancel drives RUNNING → CANCELLING → DRAINING → EXITED, terminating the child, flushing the journal, and releasing the lock"), so the test cannot be written to assert the documented behavior.

WHY THIS IS P1: same defect class as F17 — a task carries acceptance criteria that the fixed contract it depends on cannot satisfy. Left unresolved the implementer must either (a) silently drop the test, leaving cancellation during a slow BOOTSTRAPPING/RESOLVING/LAUNCHING phase undefined — and those phases include network and process-spawn work, exactly where an operator is most likely to hit Ctrl-C — or (b) unilaterally invent a state-machine edge, diverging from the contract 119.003-T owns and that 119.004-T and 119.005-T are written against. Both outcomes are worse than an explicit ruling.

RESOLUTION OPTIONS (operator decision; Stage adopted none):
(A) Add a pre-RUNNING cancellation path — e.g. `LAUNCHING → CANCELLING → DRAINING → EXITED`, ideally generalized to every post-LOCKING phase — and keep the test. Requires amending §3.2 and the 119.003-T transition table.
(B) Remove the acceptance case and state explicitly that cancellation is undefined/refused until RUNNING, documenting the operator-visible consequence.

NOTE: option (A) also discharges F22 and F18 on 119.003-T — all three are the same missing invariant (cleanup and cancellation guaranteed only from RUNNING).

STAGE ADOPTED NO RESOLUTION and changed no dependency edge. Detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-09-copilot-cli-supervisor-control-plane-review.md (Cycle 4, tenth Copilot pass).

SUPERSEDING RESOLUTION EVENT — F23 IS RESOLVED AND THIS TASK IS NOT BLOCKED (ruling D, 2026-08-12). This event supersedes the earlier "BLOCKING — F23 (P1, OPEN, NEW)" event on this log, which is preserved above as history and is NO LONGER THE CURRENT STATE.

WHAT WAS ACCEPTED. The earlier event correctly showed that this task's required "cancel during launch" test was UNSATISFIABLE: plan §3.2 defined exactly one cancellation edge (RUNNING -> CANCELLING), so a cancel arriving in LAUNCHING could only be refused as ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, contradicting this task's own stated cancellation contract. The operator adopted resolution option (A), the generalized form.

CURRENT CONTRACT. OPERATOR CANCEL IS LEGAL FROM EVERY POST-LOCKING PHASE (F18/F23 ruling) and always drives <phase> -> CANCELLING -> DRAINING -> EXITED, terminating the child if one exists, flushing the journal, and releasing the lock. Because cancel is legal from LAUNCHING, the "cancel during launch" case is now SATISFIABLE against the 119.003-T transition table instead of describing an illegal transition. As the earlier event anticipated, this same generalization also discharges F22 and F18 on 119.003-T — all three were the same missing invariant, namely that cleanup and cancellation were guaranteed only from RUNNING.

ALSO CURRENT (ruling B, 2026-08-12): this task's RESTART path — "a restart requires BOTH remaining budget AND explicit operator confirmation" — is now enumerated as the gated action `session_restart` in the FROZEN gated-action catalog owned by 118.003-T, with fallback policy USE_SAFE_DEFAULT(DECLINE_RESTART) since the restart budget already defaults to 0. Exact-set-equality tests at 118.003-T and 120.004-T mean this action can no longer be silently omitted from approval routing.

STATUS: NOT BLOCKED. Executable as written.
